battle.name: 唐收復長安之戰
battle.brief: 唐肅宗至德二載（757）十月，郭子儀率唐軍會回鶻精騎，自河中蒲州西渡蒲津，轉取華州，進逼長安，叛將安守忠開城出降，西京遂復。卡面那柄羅馬短劍並未入華，它代表的是短兵相接的母型：以盾抵格、以刺找縫，唐軍近身靠陌刀、橫刀與盾陣承襲同一套節奏。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 交戰雙方是唐廷與安史叛軍所建的偽燕。唐廷一方以西京行營的聯軍為主幹：廣平王李俶掛名元帥，郭子儀任副元帥兼行軍總制，轄朔方、河中、河東、隴右、西川諸道之兵與京畿宿衛，南蕃、西域諸國部眾亦隨軍聽用；監軍由宦官魚朝恩、程元振一系把持，使朝廷能直接駕馭外軍。回鶻（黠戛斯）可汗帳下的精騎以盟軍身分參戰，由僕固懷恩引領，戰力與唐軍合流，卻始終自成一軍，事後以繒帛、馬匹酬謝。叛軍一方是安祿山開創、安慶緒承襲的燕政權：安慶緒坐鎮洛陽、鄴城，嚴莊掌機要，安守忠屯守西京，崔乾祐守洛陽與華州，河北成德、范陽、平盧等節度使以契丹、奚、室韋騎兵為骨架，再雜以河朔與關中降附的市卒游騎。偽燕能戰之兵多為傭兵與胡騎，攻城靠雲梯、撞車，野戰以騎兵突襲見長。整體看，唐廷是兵分多路而號令歸一的聯軍，叛軍則是河北老底子加關中殘部的鬆散聯盟，各自為戰而互不接應。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Tang court and the rebel state of Yan, proclaimed by An Lushan and inherited by An Qingxu. On the Tang side the backbone was the coalition assembled in the campaign for the Western Capital: Prince Guangping Li Chu held the title of commander-in-chief, while Guo Ziyi served as deputy commander-in-chief and exercised the field command, over the levies of the Northern and Southern Circuits, of Hedong, Hexi, Longyou and Xichuan and of the capital district, with contingents of the southern and western states brought along to serve. The eunuch overseers of the army, Yu Chao'en and Cheng Yuanzhen, sat above the generals so that the court could hold the field army directly. The picked cavalry of the Uyghur, the Tiele people, took part as a treaty ally led by Pugu Huai'en; their strength was folded into the Tang order of battle while remaining a host of their own, and they were paid afterwards in silk and horses. On the Yan side stood the regime founded by An Lushan and continued by An Qingxu: An Qingxu sat at Luoyang and later Yecheng, the eunuch Yan Zhuang directed policy, An Shouzhong garrisoned the Western Capital, Cui Qianyou held Luoyang and Huazhou, and the jiedushi of Chengde, Fanyang and Pinglu in Hebei supplied the skeleton of the rebel army in Khitan, Xi and Shiwei cavalry, reinforced by hired soldiers and by volunteers and surrendered men from Hebei and Guanzhong. The fighting core of Yan was mercenary and steppe cavalry: walls were assaulted with scaling towers and battering rams, and open battle relied on mounted surprise. In sum, the Tang host was a coalition drawn from many routes but held together by one chain of command, while the rebels were a loose alliance of Hebei's old military households and the shattered remnants of Guanzhong, each fighting on its own and unable to support the others.
people: 核心人物是廣平王李俶（後即帝位為唐代宗）、行軍實際主帥郭子儀，以及先鋒大將李嗣業。李俶掛帥但年少，軍中實權落在郭子儀手上；郭子儀在關中收拾殘局、整編河東散兵，又傳出單騎入回鶻營與僕固懷恩相見之事，憑個人威望化解盟軍之間的猜疑，是全役能順利推進的關鍵。李嗣業自河中、朔方轉戰前線，以所部驍卒當先鋒破陣，唐人稱之為「陌刀之隊」；其人剛直，事後被監軍中官進讒，於本役之後被構陷斬於軍中，唐軍的突擊骨幹幾乎為之中斷。僕固懷恩出身鐵勒，父祖世代為唐將，與郭子儀私交甚篤，本役引回鶻精騎入援，功成之後卻因朝廷猜忌其權勢而與唐室生隙，日後再起兵端。安守忠為偽燕守將，見唐軍逼近、援兵不至，開城出降；安慶緒坐鎮洛陽、鄴城，接到西京失守的消息後放棄洛陽，節節北退。史思明是河北最能打的悍將，本役中按兵觀變，其後再度叛唐，成為平叛末段最難纏的對手。朝廷一方還有玄宗、肅宗父子：玄宗入蜀，肅宗即位靈武，兩人對西京的態度構成本役的政治底色。
peopleEn: The central figures are Prince Guangping Li Chu, who later took the throne as Emperor Daizong, Guo Ziyi, who actually commanded the operation in the field, and Li Siye, who led the vanguard. Li Chu bore the title of commander-in-chief but was still young, and the real authority in the army rested with Guo Ziyi, who reassembled the shattered forces in Guanzhong, reorganised the scattered troops of Hedong, and then, on the famous occasion of riding alone into the Uyghur camp to meet Pugu Huai'en, used his personal standing to dissolve the mutual suspicion between the allies; that was the single decisive reason the operation moved forward as it did. Li Siye came forward from Hedong and the Northern Circuit, breaking enemy positions with his own hard-pressed soldiers, remembered in Tang sources as the column of modao swords that opened the assault. A blunt and upright man, he was later slanderously accused by the eunuch overseers of the army and executed in camp shortly after this operation, which very nearly cut off the Tang assault at the root. Pugu Huai'en, of Tiele descent, came of a family that had served the Tang for generations and was on intimate terms with Guo Ziyi; in this operation he brought the Uyghur cavalry to the field, but after the victory the court's suspicion of his growing power put him at odds with the Tang, and he later rose in arms against it. An Shouzhong, the Yan commander holding the Western Capital, threw open the gates and surrendered when the Tang army closed in and no relief was coming. An Qingxu, at Luoyang and then Yecheng, abandoned Luoyang and fell back north stage by stage. Shi Siming, the ablest of the Yan commanders in Hebei, watched and waited during the operation and rose in revolt against the Tang again afterwards, becoming the most tenacious opponent of the closing phase of the rebellion. On the court's side stand Emperor Xuanzong and his son Suzong: Xuanzong had fled into Shu, Suzong had taken the throne at Lingwu, and the attitude of the two towards the Western Capital gave this operation its political colour.
kits: 卡面兵器是約公元前一百年前後的羅馬短劍，是羅馬軍團列陣時的標準近身兵器：它不是用來揮砍的，短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣頂住對手的攻擊，再以刺突的節奏一記一記找縫隙。劍士左手大盾、右手短劍，重心低、步幅小，刺出即收，收後再刺，所以後世講「以刺代劈」。這件兵器從未入華，也沒有出現在757年的關中戰場，但它代表的那套近戰邏輯，正是唐軍步卒所走的路。唐軍近身用陌刀：雙刃、刀身修長逾丈半，由隋制一系的裝備推演而來，長柄護手，作為軍隊集體突擊的長刀使用，其源頭仍是唐人自漢以來沿用的鉤鑼刀一脈；騎兵佩橫刀，單刃、便於腰間抽出；步卒以方盾、圓盾成列抵擋，以槊、戈補長距。防具以明光鎧為代表，胸前一片圓盤護胸，承自漢魏的兩當與鍪甲傳統，重在護住胸腹而非全身；鎧外披甲，內綴袍服，長槊手多著皮甲、札甲，禁軍精騎才用鎖子甲配長槊。攻城器械備有巢車、雲梯、攻城車與擲石機，但本役未大規模使用。遠射靠蹶張弩、單弓與唐兵通用的角弓，箭鏃以鐵為主。回鶻騎兵另有裝備體系：複合短弓拉力大、便於騎射，配彎刀、馬槊、鎖子甲，馬具輕便，利於長途奔襲後即時散開。運輸與補給靠河中的糧倉與漕運，車隊、芻粟與繒帛的供應，決定了遠征軍隊能走多快。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Roman gladius, of roughly a century before the beginning of the Common Era, the standard close-combat arm of the Roman legion in the line: it was never meant to be swung, and in close fighting it was the edge of the shield that held the enemy's blow at bay while the rhythm of the thrust looked for the gap. The legionary carried the large oval scutum in the left hand and the short sword in the right, kept his weight low and his steps short, thrust and recovered in a single movement, which is why later writers spoke of cutting by stabbing. The weapon never reached China and certainly did not appear on the Guanzhong battlefield of 757, yet the body of close-combat logic it embodies is exactly the road the Tang foot soldier walked. Tang infantry closed with the modao: a double-edged blade more than a metre and a half long, developed from the equipment regulations inherited from the Sui, with a long hilt and a hand-guard, used as the collective long-sword of an assault, and tracing its origin to the hooked blade-and-spear line the Tang had carried down from the Han. Cavalry rode with the hengdao, single-edged and easy to draw at the waist, while infantry stood in files of square and round shields, with the spear and the ge covering the longer reaches. Armour was represented by the Mingguang piece, its chest furnished with a round disc guarding the torso, inherited from the liangdang and helmet tradition of the Han and Wei and concerned above all with covering chest and belly rather than the whole body; over the armour went a coat, and within it were worn the mail and lamellar pieces, the spearmen largely in leather or lacquered plate, while only the picked cavalry of the imperial guards carried mail together with the long spear. The siege train included the nest-tower, scaling ladders, siege wagons and stone-throwers, though this operation never brought them into serious use. At range the army relied on the strong-drawn crossbow, the single bow and the composite bow common among Tang troops, with iron heads. The Uyghur horse carried a system of its own: a compact composite bow of heavy draw suited to shooting from the saddle, a curved sabre, the lance, mail and light harness, allowing long rides and instant dispersal. Transport and supply ran through the depots of Hezhong and the river transport; the wagon trains, fodder and silk that followed the army decided how fast a far-flung column could move.
tactics: 本役的戰術主軸不是強攻，而是壓迫與受降。九月，唐軍在河中一帶集結，先鋒李嗣業部與回鶻騎兵先行出擊，掃清華州一線，為大軍打開關中的通道；主力自蒲津渡河，沿渭水東岸北道推進，抵長安城東十里一線下寨，隨即合圍城東與城北，只留西面通道，任叛軍自行判斷去留。叛軍此時糧道已被唐軍切斷，援軍遠在河北，內部安守忠與嚴莊等互不信任，防守全靠城垣與守卒硬撐，已無反擊的條件。攻城沒有大舉強攻：唐軍備好雲梯、巢車與擲石，也做過夜襲與火攻的準備，但終究沒有派上用場，最後是安守忠開門出降，唐軍入城接管府庫、城防與印信文書。回鶻騎兵在過程中擔任兩角：一是前哨與側翼警戒，監視洛陽方向與潰散之兵，二是隨主力逼近城下的機動打擊。城破之後，唐軍不急於追擊，而是分兵守城、整頓軍紀、接收降卒，再乘勝東進洛陽，逼安慶緒北撤。整場戰役反映的仍是唐廷的老戰略：先以騎兵與前鋒奪取節點，再以大軍壓迫，最後用政治手段收編守軍，把一場攻城戰變成一場接收戰。
tacticsEn: The tactical axis of this operation was not a storm of the walls but pressure and surrender. In September the Tang forces mustered around Hezhong; the vanguard under Li Siye and the Uyghur cavalry moved out first, clearing the line through Huazhou and opening the approach into Guanzhong for the main body. The main army crossed the river at Pujin and advanced north along the east bank of the Wei, established itself in a line ten li from the eastern gate of Chang'an, and then closed around the east and north of the city, leaving the western road open so that the rebels could judge for themselves what to do. By then the rebels' supply line had been cut by the Tang, their relief army lay far away in Hebei, and the Yan commanders were divided among themselves; defence rested entirely on the walls and a garrison with no means of counterattacking. There was no serious assault: ladders, nest-towers and stone-throwers were prepared and plans for night attack and fire were made, but none of them was used, and in the end An Shouzhong opened the gates and surrendered, after which the Tang army entered and took over the treasuries, the defences and the seals and documents of the administration. The Uyghur cavalry played two roles in the operation: they formed the advance guard and flank screen, watching the road towards Luoyang and picking up fugitives, and they provided mobile striking force as the main body closed on the walls. Once the city had fallen the Tang did not rush forward in pursuit; they split off to garrison the city, restore discipline, take in the surrendered, and then drove east to Luoyang, pressing An Qingxu back to the north. The operation illustrates the old Tang formula: cavalry and vanguard seize the nodal points, the main army applies the pressure, and the garrison is then taken in by political means, turning a siege into a takeover.
data: 兵力方面可核的數字大致如下：《舊唐書》記郭子儀所統大軍約二十萬，其中唐軍十五萬上下，回鶻精騎萬餘，其餘為朔方、河中、西域諸道之眾；偽燕方面，長安守軍為精兵萬餘，洛陽一線兵力在十萬上下，河北各節度使名下所報兵數更為龐大。安史亂起時曾有十四節度使統兵五十餘萬的說法，但那批兵多為臨時糾集、彼此不屬，能戰者有限；潼關一役，唐廷關中精兵二十萬在靈寶數日之內全潰，說明兵額與戰力不能直接換算。距離上，河中蒲州至長安約四百餘里，崔乾祐據守的華州正在途中，唐軍先取華州再進兵城下。時間上，至德二載九月集兵發進，十月抵達城下並收復西京，十一月進軍東都、收復洛陽，一個月內連下兩京，是整個安史之亂中唐軍推進最快的一次。消耗方面，潼關敗後關中精銳盡喪，長安城內的府庫兵械多為叛軍所掠，兩京初復時軍器不足，需自隴右、河東調發；回鶻以精騎出動，唐廷以繒帛、馬匹相酬，是這場戰役中另一筆可觀的物資流向。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. The Old Book of Tang records that the army under Guo Ziyi numbered about two hundred thousand in all, of which some one hundred and fifty thousand were Tang troops, upwards of ten thousand were picked Uyghur cavalry, and the rest were drawn from the Northern and Southern Circuits, from Hezhong and from the western states. On the Yan side the garrison of the Western Capital was in the region of ten thousand picked troops, the forces around Luoyang numbered on the order of a hundred thousand, and the totals reported by the Hebei jiedushi were far larger. When the rebellion began there was talk of fourteen jiedushi with more than five hundred thousand men, but those troops were hastily gathered and answerable to nobody, and only a fraction could really fight; at Tong Pass the twenty thousand picked troops of the Western Capital were destroyed in a few days at Lingbao, which shows that nominal numbers cannot be converted directly into fighting power. As to distance: from Puzhou in Hezhong to Chang'an is about four hundred and more li, and Huazhou, held by Cui Qianyou, lay on the road, so the Tang took Huazhou first and then moved on the city. As to time: the army mustered and set out in the ninth month, reached the walls and retook the Western Capital in the tenth month, and advanced on the Eastern Capital and retook Luoyang in the eleventh month — two capitals in a single month, the fastest advance the Tang achieved at any point in the rebellion. As to wastage: after the defeat at Tong Pass the picked troops of Guanzhong were gone, and the stores and arms in the captured capital had been carried off by the rebels, so that when the two capitals were retaken the army was short of equipment and had to draw on Longyou and Hedong; and since the Uyghur had brought their picked cavalry into the field, the court paid them in silk and horses, which was the other considerable flow of materiel in this operation.
cause: 戰爭的根子在安祿山於755年冬天以奉密詔討楊國忠為名在范陽起兵，兩年之間打下洛陽、潼關與西京，天寶盛世的局面為之崩解。756年玄宗入蜀，太子李亨在靈武即位，是為肅宗，改元至德，朝廷在靈州、陝西一帶重建，藉朔方軍與河東軍重新集結兵馬。長安陷落之後，叛軍以洛陽為中樞，卻始終解決不了河北與關中兩地的聯繫：河北諸節度使各擁重兵、擁兵自重，關中只餘破敗之城與缺糧的守軍。757年春夏，唐廷在河東戰線站穩腳跟，李光弼、郭子儀相繼打通太原、潞州與洛陽的通道，叛軍西進之路被截斷；肅宗於是下令以廣平王為元帥、郭子儀為副元帥，會同回鶻兵收復兩京。對唐廷而言，收復西京不只是軍事動作，更是名分之爭：西京一旦回來，朝廷才有正統的所在，也才談得上再向河北用兵；對叛軍而言，兩京若失，就只剩河朔一隅的割據。最終促使安守忠開城的，還是極現實的算盤：援軍不至、糧道斷絕、城內人心已散，硬守只會玉石俱焚。
causeEn: The roots of the war lie in An Lushan's rising in the winter of 755 at Fanyang, under the pretext of a secret imperial order to punish Yang Guozhong, and in the two years that followed his seizure of Luoyang, of Tong Pass and of the Western Capital, which shattered the fabric of the Tianbao prosperity. In 756 Xuanzong fled into Shu and his son Li Heng took the throne at Lingwu as Suzong, changed the era name to Zhide and rebuilt the court in the Lingzhou and Shaanxi area, remustering troops through the Northern Circuit and Hedong armies. After the fall of the capital the rebels made Luoyang their centre, yet never solved the connection between Hebei and Guanzhong: the Hebei jiedushi each held heavy forces and refused to be controlled, while Guanzhong had nothing left but a ruined city and a hungry garrison. Through the spring and summer of 757 the court stabilised on the Hedong front; Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi successively reopened the routes by Taoyuan, Luzhou and Luoyang, cutting off the rebels' advance to the west. Suzong therefore ordered Prince Guangping to command and Guo Ziyi to serve as deputy, and to retake both capitals together with the Uyghur horse. For the Tang court, the recovery of the Western Capital was not merely a military operation but a question of legitimacy: with the capital back, the court had a seat of legitimate authority and could think of resuming the war in Hebei. For the rebels, the loss of both capitals would leave nothing but the semi-independent corner of Hebei. What finally induced An Shouzhong to open the gates was a very practical calculation: no relief was coming, the supply line was cut, and the garrison had lost heart, so that a stubborn defence would only destroy both sides.
impact: 兩京的收復是安史之亂的轉折點，卻不是終點。政治上，西京重歸唐室，肅宗的政令自此有了真正的腹地，玄宗於同年冬天自蜀返京，父子先後入城，唐朝的禮儀、官署與檔案重新接續；軍事上，安慶緒退保鄴城，史思明以河北兵再起，763年才平定，前線始終在河北與河東之間拉鋸。制度上，經此一役，節度使擁有的兵權進一步坐大，河朔諸鎮自此形同外包，藩鎮割據的格局在此後百餘年裡逐步成形；與此同時，回鶻深度介入唐室內政，唐廷對外族的倚賴與防範同時加深，僕固懷恩的結局即為例證。軍制上，朔方軍與鄜原等西北精兵成為朝廷倚重的骨幹，禁軍與方鎮之間的比重被重新調整，募兵、降附之眾與蕃兵的編制在實戰中被重新整合。兵器與戰術上，陌刀、長槊與盾的組合在唐軍中定型，近身戰仍以列盾而進、以刀槊取隙為要訣，正是卡面那柄羅馬短劍所代表的刺擊傳統在東方的對應物，儘管兩套傳統從未相遇。
impactEn: The recovery of the two capitals was the turning point of the An Lushan rebellion, though not its end. Politically the Western Capital returned to the Tang and Suzong's decrees once more had a real hinterland; Xuanzong came back from Shu in the winter of the same year and the father and son entered the city in turn, and the rituals, offices and archives of the Tang were reconnected. Militarily An Qingxu fell back on Yecheng, Shi Siming rose again with the Hebei armies, and the war was not settled until 763, the front line running back and forth between Hebei and Hedong throughout. Institutionally, the war left the jiedushi in command of yet more troops; the Hebei circuits became in effect foreign enclaves, and the pattern of regional militarism that would characterise the next century and more took shape. At the same time the Uyghur were drawn deep into Tang politics, and the court's reliance on the foreigners and its wariness of them both grew, as the fate of Pugu Huai'en showed. In military organisation the picked northern formations of the Northern Circuit and the Fuyuan troops became the backbone the court depended upon, the balance between the imperial guards and the regional commands was readjusted, and the raising of recruited, incorporated and steppe troops was reworked in the light of what the fighting actually required. In weapons and tactics the pairing of the modao, the long spear and the shield was settled into Tang practice, and close combat still turned on advancing behind shields and taking the opening with blade and spear — exactly the thrusting tradition represented by the Roman gladius on the card, though the two traditions never met.
result: 至德二載十月，唐軍進抵長安城下，叛將安守忠開門出降，西京收復；十一月，軍鋒東指，崔乾祐棄洛陽北走，安慶緒退保鄴城，東都亦復。兩京既得，唐廷封郭子儀為汾陽郡王，重整府庫、恢復編制與官吏，接收降卒與歸順官吏，封存叛軍所掠的印信文書，這套動作把一次軍事勝利轉成了行政上的接管。代宗即位之後的失誤卻在此役之後接連顯現：李嗣業被構斬於軍，先鋒骨幹受損；監軍中官權力膨脹，讒言不斷；史思明很快再度舉兵，兩京得而復失。回鶻盟軍在取得酬謝後北返，本役開啟的借外兵收復失地模式，成為唐廷此後對付叛軍的常規手段，也埋下外族干政與藩鎮坐大的雙重後果。整體看，唐收復長安之戰是安史之亂中唐軍第一次成建制地奪回首都，勝在攻勢與盟軍配合之順，敗在未能乘勢掃平河北；它改變了戰爭的地理重心，卻沒有改變戰爭的結局。
resultEn: In the tenth month of Zhide two, the Tang army reached the walls of Chang'an, the Yan commander An Shouzhong opened the gates and surrendered, and the Western Capital was retaken. In the eleventh month the army turned east, Cui Qianyou abandoned Luoyang and withdrew north, An Qingxu fell back on Yecheng, and the Eastern Capital was recovered as well. With both capitals in hand the court raised Guo Ziyi to the title of Prince of Fenyang, reorganised the treasuries, restored the registers and the officials, took in the surrendered and the officials who came over, and sealed up the seals and documents the rebels had carried away, and that series of acts turned a military victory into an administrative takeover. The mistakes that followed Daizong's accession, however, became visible in quick succession after this operation: Li Siye was framed and executed in camp, damaging the backbone of the assault; the eunuch overseers of the army grew in power and slander followed on slander; and Shi Siming soon raised arms anew, so that the two capitals were lost a second time. The Uyghur allies, having received their payment, returned north, and the pattern of borrowing foreign troops to recover lost ground that this operation inaugurated became a regular expedient of the Tang in the war that followed, while sowing both the danger of foreign intervention and the seed of the regional commands that grew in power from it. Seen as a whole, the recapture of Chang'an was the first time the Tang army took a capital back in organised formation during the rebellion; it was won by the momentum of the advance and by the smooth working of the allied horse, and lost by the failure to follow it up into Hebei. It changed the geographical centre of the war without changing its outcome.
